request: the delivery target guard and the post-import hook behaviour

defects.description: WebhookClient.prepare runs the internal-address rules against the raw URL text instead of the parsed hostname, so a URL whose text starts with a public host but whose authority is a loopback address is posted, although Relay.enqueue and the dispatcher both validate with assertTarget, which checks the parsed hostname.

trigger.expected: D1 Relay.deliverNow({url: 'https://example.com@127.0.0.1:8080/hook'}) -> blocked egress blocked: 127.0.0.1 is an internal address

defects.why_missed: Every internal target the suite refuses puts the dotted address at the front of the URL, which is the shape the raw-text rules match, so the check looks like it is reading the host the request reaches.

defects.description: The post-import hook joins the interpreter, the hook script and the payload name into one command string and runs it through a shell, while src/hooks/runner.js validates every argument with assertHookArgument and spawns without a shell; the payload name is a plain token by contract, so a name carrying a semicolon runs a second command.

trigger.expected: D2 runPostImportHook('payload.json; printf relay-injected') -> blocked unsafe hook argument: payload.json; printf relay-injected
trigger.actual: D2 runPostImportHook('payload.json; printf relay-injected') -> stdout "tagged payload.json\nrelay-injected"

defects.why_missed: The suite runs the hook with payload.json, where a shell and a spawn produce the same output, and checks assertHookArgument on its own, so the one path that never calls it is exercised only on a name the shell reads as a single word.
